title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-07
lineage: [SBD MR > C > D > CD] + [AUD MC > 4C > CD patches]

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with a muddy early mix that clears up, delivering a solid 1970 Fillmore West set highlighted by Sawmill and a fiery China Cat > I Know You Rider.
ai_review.review: The performance is generally praised for its energy, especially the country‑flavored Sawmill on pedal steel and the high‑octane China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence, while later cuts like Black Peter and High Time also stand out. Recording-wise the tape starts out muddy with balance and monitor issues, but by the second half it settles into decent soundboard quality. Overall the show is enjoyable for fans of this era despite the technical hiccups.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers note strong musical moments (show weight ~70%) and a recording that improves after an initial muddy section (recording weight ~30%); combined weighted score yields around 3.5‑4 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early portion is muddy with balance problems and delayed stage mic switch; bass can sound boomy; later songs achieve clearer soundboard mix but some cuts remain.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: One long set with an early monitor issue and a brief set break; the band recovers into tighter playing, though some tracks are cut or end abruptly.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel work on Sawmill described as joyous; his soloing is noted as beginning to explore new possibilities.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass reported as too boomy early in the mix before the soundboard levels settle.
